# Debrief: Argo CD

These clips show an Argo CD team how to preview pull request diffs fast, add AI and MCP tooling, adopt GitOps and rollouts, and avoid a gateway migration pitfall that broke Argo CD paths. ([Argo CD: Previewing Pull Request Changes in SECONDS! · 10:49](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fcajag5di68&t=649s); [The 10x DevOps Engineer’s Toolkit: Argo CD + AI-Driven MCP Automation · 7:52](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iC15zeOLZQA&t=472s); [From FTP To Argo CD & Argo Rollouts: An Adoption History Inside a Corp · 12:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wrek7kjrcs0&t=737s); [From ingress-nginx to Envoy Gateway at Zapier: The Benefits, Challenges, and Migration Lessons That Matter · 8:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kIj2U13VZJY&t=531s))

## Top 3 takeaways

1. Argo CD diff preview using a real, slimmed-down namespace-scoped Argo CD gave about 5-second pull request previews across roughly 1,000 applications, giving accurate previews and confidence when merging to production. ([Argo CD: Previewing Pull Request Changes in SECONDS! · 10:49](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fcajag5di68&t=649s))
2. Templated setups need extra work for previews: rendering only the applications and clusters affected by a change cut rendering sharply, and custom plugins or Helm binaries can be supported. ([Argo CD: Previewing Pull Request Changes in SECONDS! · 16:16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fcajag5di68&t=976s); [Argo CD: Previewing Pull Request Changes in SECONDS! · 12:57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fcajag5di68&t=777s))
3. MCP for Argo CD is a new open source server whose tools map one-to-one to CLI and UI actions, including sync, logs and live manifests, so AI can inspect and operate applications. ([The 10x DevOps Engineer’s Toolkit: Argo CD + AI-Driven MCP Automation · 7:52](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iC15zeOLZQA&t=472s))

## Action items

- [ ] Try Argo CD diff preview on pull requests, using a namespace-scoped, slimmed-down Argo CD with self-hosted runners, and measure preview time on your main repository. ([Argo CD: Previewing Pull Request Changes in SECONDS! · 10:49](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fcajag5di68&t=649s))
- [ ] If your applications are rendered from Helm or Kustomize layers, limit pull request rendering to only the applications and clusters whose files changed. ([Argo CD: Previewing Pull Request Changes in SECONDS! · 16:16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fcajag5di68&t=976s); [Argo CD: Previewing Pull Request Changes in SECONDS! · 12:57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fcajag5di68&t=777s))
- [ ] If you move to Envoy Gateway, test that encoded slashes in Argo CD paths are preserved, setting the escape slashes action to keep unchanged to avoid 404s. ([From ingress-nginx to Envoy Gateway at Zapier: The Benefits, Challenges, and Migration Lessons That Matter · 8:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kIj2U13VZJY&t=531s))

## Watch together (8 min)

1. [Argo CD: Previewing Pull Request Changes in SECONDS! · 10:49](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fcajag5di68&t=649s) (1:19), Dag Bjerre Andersen, Sergey Shevchenko: Concrete lockdown-mode setup and 5-second pull request previews at scale.
2. [Argo CD: Previewing Pull Request Changes in SECONDS! · 16:16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fcajag5di68&t=976s) (1:19), Dag Bjerre Andersen, Sergey Shevchenko: Shows how to scope rendering for templated, multi-cluster setups.
3. [The 10x DevOps Engineer’s Toolkit: Argo CD + AI-Driven MCP Automation · 7:52](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iC15zeOLZQA&t=472s) (1:19), Alexander Matyushentsev, Leonardo Luz Almeida: Explains what the Argo CD MCP server can do today.
4. [From ingress-nginx to Envoy Gateway at Zapier: The Benefits, Challenges, and Migration Lessons That Matter · 8:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kIj2U13VZJY&t=531s) (2:27), Kalen Wessel: Warns about gateway path normalization breaking Argo CD with 404s.
5. [From FTP To Argo CD & Argo Rollouts: An Adoption History Inside a Corp · 12:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wrek7kjrcs0&t=737s) (1:19), Alfonso Ming, Meritxell Rodríguez: Clear GitOps rationale: declarative state, drift correction, and rollback.
